name: Prone T-Raise
description: The prone T-raise is a posterior shoulder and middle trapezius exercise performed lying face down with arms extended directly to the sides, forming a T shape. This horizontal abduction movement targets the posterior deltoid and middle trapezius and is a staple corrective exercise for improving shoulder blade retraction strength and postural alignment.

execution.starting_position: Lie face down on the floor or an incline bench with arms extended directly to the sides, perpendicular to the torso, forming a T. Thumbs point toward the ceiling.
execution.setup_instructions: No equipment needed for bodyweight. Add light dumbbells (1–3 kg) for increased load. Can be done over an incline bench for greater range of motion.
steps: Step 1: Lie face down with arms extended to the sides in a T shape. Thumbs point up.
Step 2: Depress and retract the shoulder blades.
Step 3: Exhale and raise both arms toward the ceiling, squeezing the middle traps and rear delts.
Step 4: Hold at the top 1–2 seconds, then inhale and lower back to the floor.
execution.breathing_instructions: Exhale on the raise; inhale on the return.
common_mistakes: Letting the shoulder blades wing outward — actively retract them during the raise
Using upper trap shrugging instead of mid-trap retraction
safety_considerations: Very light load only — this is a corrective and endurance exercise
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Raise arms until middle traps are maximally contracted; they will not go very high.
coaching_cues: Squeeze your shoulder blades together as you raise
Thumbs up keeps the shoulder in a safe external rotation position
